hints: Start by recalling what makes isotopes different from each other, and what stays exactly the same.
Remember the two common chlorine isotopes are $^{35}\text{Cl}$ and $^{37}\text{Cl}$, so count their protons, neutrons and nucleons.
Link electron arrangement to chemical behaviour to decide if their reactions will be identical despite the mass difference.
walkthrough:
**Recall the definition of isotopes**

Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. For chlorine, both isotopes have 17 protons but one has 18 neutrons and the other has 20 neutrons.

$$ \text{isotopes: same } p, \text{ different } n $$

**Check mass and nucleon number**

Mass comes mainly from protons + neutrons, which are called nucleons. Since neutron number differs, total nucleon number differs, so mass differs too.

$$ ^{35}\text{Cl}: 17p + 18n = 35 \text{ nucleons} $$
$$ ^{37}\text{Cl}: 17p + 20n = 37 \text{ nucleons} $$
This confirms statements 1 and 2 are both correct.

**Check chemical reactions**

Chemical reactions depend on electronic configuration, especially outer shell electrons, not on neutrons. Both isotopes have the same arrangement $2,8,7$, so they react identically.

$$ \text{same electrons} \rightarrow \text{same chemistry} $$
This confirms statement 3 is also correct, so 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct. Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all true. The isotopes $^{35}\text{Cl}$ and $^{37}\text{Cl}$ have different neutron numbers, so different nucleon numbers and different masses, but identical electron arrangements so identical chemistry.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination leaves out statement 3. Students sometimes think different mass means different chemistry, but chemical behaviour is controlled by electrons, which are the same in isotopes.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination leaves out statement 1. Students sometimes confuse mass number with something else, but different numbers of neutrons must give different masses because neutrons have significant mass.
options.D: Incorrect. This suggests only one statement is true. This comes from forgetting the definition of isotopes. Remember: same protons, different neutrons gives different nucleons, different mass, same electrons and same reactions.
